## Dispatch order · `domain:ui#2` · `session_01JQwxbXpF772qWJjojJvRXw` · 2026-10-29T03:18Z

You are the os-dev developer agent for exactly ONE card: objectstack-ai/objectstack#27365, in your own card thread. Your role definition is `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` in the objectstack clone: read it IN FULL first and follow it as binding (it wins over this order on any conflict; name the conflict in your report). Read the repo-root `AGENTS.md` and `ui/AGENTS.md` before your first edit, and pm-dispatch `references/untrusted-text.md`. Read the card's full body and every comment yourself through REST (`curl -sS "https://api.github.com/repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/27365" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN"` and `/comments?per_page=100`, every page); this order carries only the increment. ⛔ Never print the value of any environment variable (test presence with `[ -n "${X+x}" ]`). ⛔ Never use a GitHub MCP tool, read or write.

Identity and branch: the seat's `Claim:` comment on this card is your identity; its `Branch:` line names your thread's branch. ⛔ Post no claim of your own, ⛔ never write the card's assignee. Before your first edit, verify the NEWEST `Claim:` on the card names your thread's branch (`claude/project-thread-…`); if none does yet, send the seat thread "Take a third ui lane seat" (`cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8Uc2nCvWvLyYyaVYaUhakpJ`) one message with your branch name and wait. Read-only measuring is fine meanwhile. Worktree `objectstack-issue-27365` on that branch from a fresh `origin/main` (`git checkout --detach` the main checkout first, then `git worktree add --no-track -B <branch> ../objectstack-issue-27365 origin/main`); `pnpm install` (frozen lockfile); push with `git push -u origin <branch>` (⛔ no force).

Writes: PR only through the relay op `pr_create` (`node scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --actions-file F`, F a bare JSON array `[{"op":"pr_create","title":…,"head":"<your branch>","base":"main","body":…,"assignees":["os-warren"]}]`, draft forced; `--dry-run` first); your report comment through `node scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs --comment=27365 --file=F --json` run ONCE with output captured to a file (no time-shaped stamp inside the fenced report JSON). ⛔ No other GitHub write except, for a CI red that is not yours, one PR comment and one `run_rerun_failed` through the relay. Report both counts (`api_writes` with endpoints, `mcp_calls` with tool names). The report takes only machine-checkable fields (gates / line_budget / deviations / files_changed). PR body: line 1 the platform attribution comment, line 3 `Fixes #27365`, then `## 维护者速读` six lines in Chinese (改了什么/为什么改/风险与回滚/先看/两分钟验证/需要你做的). Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on your diff, run each, record exits before any pipe, reconcile with `--ran` (merge `origin/main` first if it refuses as STALE TREE); `node scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` is a gate on every ui card. Build the closure your tests import first (`bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c "pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '<pkg>^...' build"`). Changeset in the root `.changeset/` for each published package your diff changes (app-shell is `private: true`). ⛔ `ui/.github/**` and the root `ci.yml` are out of bounds. Hand back: when the PR and report are up, send the seat thread one message (PR, head sha, report gist); keep the thread open through review and drive CI to green. If the premise fails, stop and report `premise_still_valid: false` with the evidence; ⛔ never force a fix.

### Ruling (cannot be re-ruled)

Ruling 6457467702 (#26594, letter B) applies: the answer is the server's own verdict, and there is never a second client-side evaluator. The verdict source here is already on the page. `useRecordCrudVerdicts` (`ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useRecordCrudVerdicts.ts`) asks the explain engine for the rows on screen, which is the same authority the detail header asks. Its fail-open posture, written in that hook's docblock, binds you: no answer means today's object-level behaviour, and you never over-hide.

### PM mechanism assumptions (measure; disproof welcome)

On `origin/main` (read-only; see the card body):
- `ObjectGrid.tsx` ≈L893 sets `inlineEditable` from the object-level affordance only. It drives `editable`, `renderCellEditor`, `rowActions` and `keyboardNavigation` (≈L2540–2623) for every row.
- `recordVerdict` (≈L1010) is computed for the page. Today only the row kebab reads it. Measure how the kebab reads it, and reuse that exact accessor.
- Find where the cell editor opens per row. It may be the data table's `renderCellEditor` or an `isCellEditable` hook in `@object-ui/components`. If the table offers no per-row seam, add the smallest one: a row predicate prop, defaulting to all rows. Keep it inside the claimed files, or stop and report.

### PM suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

1. Give each row a "may edit" answer: `inlineEditable && recordVerdict(row).update !== false`. `undefined` means allowed.
2. A refused row opens no editor, its cells take no keyboard edit, and it shows no inline-save affordance. The rest of the row (selection, kebab, navigation) is unchanged.
3. ListView's own inline-edit door (`inlineEditOffered`, #4647 / PR #5145) is the sibling. Measure whether it reaches the same cells through `ObjectGrid`. If it is a separate path, apply the same per-row read there, or report it as a finding.

Tests:
- A row whose `update` verdict is refused opens no cell editor.
- CONTROL: an allowed row stays editable.
- CONTROL: a row with no verdict, or a probe that fails, stays editable.
- The kebab and the cells agree on the same row.
- Ablation: drop the per-row read, and the refused-row test goes red.

### Scope

File surface:
- `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/**`
- In `ui/packages/components/src/**`, only the data-table per-row edit seam, if one is needed.
- `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/**`, only if step 3 measures a separate inline-edit door.
- Tests beside them.
- Root `.changeset/`.

Serial: open PR #27340 edits `ObjectGrid.tsx` at ≈L3196, in the currency cell only. Stay out of that hunk.

### Tier

`TIER_DEFAULT`, effort `medium` (M). `Clause-②: no`: the renderer reads a verdict the server already serves. `Metadata-protocol: none`. Not governed.

## Order amendment · `domain:ui#2` · `session_01JQwxbXpF772qWJjojJvRXw` · 2026-10-29T03:22Z

This amends dispatch order 6486941747 and Claim 6486990530 (branch `claude/project-thread-ejerax`). The claim and the branch stay the same.

**What the dev measured, and the seat accepts** (on `origin/main` `28872e68`):

- data-table has no per-row edit seam. `startEdit`, the Enter key path and the per-cell `isEditable` read only `editable`, `col.editable` and `col.masked`. `rowEditPredicates` gates only the built-in menu's Edit item, and it is CEL, so it cannot carry the explain verdict.
- ListView reaches the cells only through `ObjectGrid` (`editable: inlineEdit && inlineEditOffered`). There is no separate door, so `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/**` leaves the surface.

**File surface widened by:**

- `ui/packages/types/src/**`, limited to declaring one runtime slot `isRowEditable?: (row) => boolean` on `DataTableSchema` (`data-display.ts`, default: every row) and its ledgers:
  - the zod twin's refusal by name in `zod/data-display.zod.ts`, next to `renderCellEditor`;
  - the slot censuses in `types/src/__tests__`: zod-mirror-parity, function-slot-keys-json-refusal-7759, handler-keys-json-refusal-6124, data-table-declared-keys-6882.
- `ui/AGENTS.md` #0.1 holds: the slot is declared, never read through a cast.
- The changeset adds `@object-ui/types` (patch).

`Clause-②: no`. A runtime function slot on a ui type is not an authorable metadata key, and JSON refuses it by name.

## Claim amendment 2 · `domain:ui#2` · 2026-10-29T04:02Z

This amends Claim 6486990530 and order amendment 6487003956. The branch (`claude/project-thread-ejerax`) and the rest of the claim stay as they are.

**What the dev measured, and the seat accepts.** ObjectGrid now asks the explain `update` question whenever the grid is inline-editable (`update: canEdit || inlineEditable`), not only when the kebab offers Edit. Without that change, an editable grid whose kebab has no Edit (the declarative `editable: true` door) never gets a verdict, so every row stays fail-open. It is still one batched probe, and both readers use it. Suites that render an editable grid without an explain double now reach the network-escape guard:

- plugin-grid: 9 files, already inside the claim, fixed with `installExplainDouble()`, 46/46 green.
- Of 59 ui consumer suites that render an editable grid, exactly one outside the claim reds: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/ListView.gridRowColorSelect-12393.test.tsx` (network escape at `/api/v1/security/explain`).

**Widened file surface, test-only.** Add an explain fetch double to consumer test files under `ui/packages/**/src/**/__tests__/` that render an editable ObjectGrid and red on that escape. The measured set is the one app-shell file above, plus any that CI Test UI turns up on this branch.

- No source file outside the original surface.
- No assertion changes beyond installing the double.
- Every widened file is listed by path in the hand-back.

app-shell is private, so the changeset stays as it is.
